name: Gabriele D'Annunzio
role: Italian poet, soldier and Comandante of the Regency of Carnaro at Fiume (1919-1920)
summary: D'Annunzio was a poet turned ultranationalist who campaigned for Italy's entry into the First World War and in 1919 seized Fiume with veterans, ruling it as a charismatic Comandante. The Charter of Carnaro he promulgated, drafted with the syndicalist De Ambris, combined universal suffrage, women's equality, recall and referendums with corporatist bodies and a social view of property. His later years were spent at Lake Garda, apart from Mussolini's government.

notes: Charter answers rest on a text drafted by De Ambris and promulgated by D'Annunzio, so they are medium at most; it was never implemented, and where his rule as Commandant is on record (Snowden) it answers instead of the Charter's words. Searched: economy, government, society, world, liberty, culture, means. Blocked or unavailable and not cited: the 1914-1918-online encyclopedia (bot check), Italian Wikisource text of his 1915 orations, Britannica. His own speeches (Quarto, 1915) and later positions (opposing a German alliance, 1937-38) were not found in an open primary source, so those statements stay null.
